record.title: Repeated materials campaigns report a shared frontier and a common-mode structure error
record.summary: A preprint compares 16 one-week autonomous materials-discovery campaigns given the same 12,499-entry metal-organic-framework database, methane-storage objective and pinned protocol. The authors report divergent search strategies but convergence near 200 cm³/cm³, with an independent calculation placing its nine best structures among agent reports. However, 15 of 16 campaigns also selected an audit-excluded incomplete structure whose missing anions created artificial pore volume. Enforced checks improved fresh-run reproduction from 1/8 to 8/8 in the tested subset but did not detectably improve conclusion validity.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In 16 sessions of one model-harness configuration, authors report convergence near 200 cm³/cm³ for methane storage, while 15/16 also selected an audit-excluded incomplete structure; enforced checks raised fresh-run reproduction from 1/8 to 8/8 in the checked subset without detectably improving conclusion validity.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper’s author-reported results do not establish independent reproduction or broader deployment impact.

evidence_gaps.description: The campaign results and structural audit have not been independently reproduced.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported behavior generalizes, repeated agent campaigns could be useful for finding robust regions of a search space, while shared input defects can make apparent convergence misleading. The evidence is a single-model, single-harness study on one frozen materials database, so broader transfer is unestablished.
limitations: The preprint reports author-run results; the research desk did not reproduce the campaigns or validate structures.
All campaigns share one model-harness configuration, frozen database, objective and protocol, so the results do not establish cross-model robustness.
The abstract reports convergence in a database search regime, not synthesized materials or measured methane-storage performance.

technical.claimed_result: In 16 sessions of one model-harness configuration, authors report convergence near 200 cm³/cm³ for methane storage, while 15/16 also selected an audit-excluded incomplete structure; enforced checks raised fresh-run reproduction from 1/8 to 8/8 in the checked subset without detectably improving conclusion validity.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv primary record establishes that the authors report this method and these results; the research desk did not independently establish experimental outcomes.
technical.mechanism: Repeated independently initialized agent sessions search a shared frozen materials database under the same objective and pinned protocol; authors compare search strategies, candidate overlap and separate structural validity checks.
technical.regime: One model-harness configuration; 12,499 frozen metal-organic framework database entries; methane-storage objective; one-week budget; 16 sessions. Eight built 2,253 hypothetical structures. The abstract’s independent porous-region calculation found nine best structures among agent reports.
technical.strongest_baseline: Repeated sessions and an independent calculation of the database porous region; no comparison across model families or fresh database collections is reported in the abstract.

brief.title: Repeated materials campaigns report a shared frontier and a common-mode structure error
brief.why_it_matters: Repeated runs can reveal both stable signals and errors inherited from shared data. This bounded study shows why replication across agents does not by itself establish that a candidate is physically valid when all runs use the same database and protocol.
